title: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B RedHatAI NVFP4 on vLLM — the SM121 kernel trap
slug_note: A documented negative result: NVFP4 of the 122B decodes at 16.6 tok/s on Spark, slower than INT4, because FP4 CUTLASS kernels do not run on SM121 yet.

engine.config: stock vLLM on a single DGX Spark

requirements.notes: Fits a single Spark; the problem is kernel support, not capacity.

steps.text: Serve the RedHatAI NVFP4 checkpoint with stock vLLM on one Spark
Expect FP4 kernels to fall back; measure before trusting the quant label

measurements.method: single DGX Spark, vLLM, single stream
measurements.note: 'slower than INT4 because FP4 CUTLASS kernels don't work on SM121 yet'.

caveats: Keep this entry precisely because it is slow: it is the counter-example to 'NVFP4 is always faster' on Blackwell-mini silicon.
Kernel support moves; re-check vLLM/FlashInfer SM121 FP4 status before deleting this row.

sources.note: NVIDIA developer forum thread with the measurement
